rationale: enc-rc4 is a Trimaran kernel: a tiny set of very hot functions dominated by a tight byte-manipulation loop (RC4 PRGA/KSA) with no function-pointer usage and negligible code size, so the priority is arithmetic-level transformation with minimal loop-body overhead. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain and the lowest cost/risk weights because instruction substitution obscures the byte-wise XOR/swap arithmetic at near-zero runtime and size cost with essentially no correctness risk — ideal for a hot loop. FLA and BCF are strongly penalized (RuntimeCost 1.0/0.9): flattening the single dominant loop and injecting bogus branches would multiply execution time on the program's hottest code path and bloat a deliberately tiny kernel, outweighing their good security scores. IBR is kept low-moderate for the same hot-path reason, applied only where branch density justifies it. SPLIT is favored as a cheap enabler that increases basic-block granularity and improves the yield of other transformations at negligible cost. ICALL and IGV are weakly weighted since the benchmark has few indirect-call or global-variable sites, so feature matching would rarely trigger them anyway, and both carry nonzero indirect-dispatch overhead in the tight loop.
